page_title: A Good Time — Make room for what matters
description: Gentle, context-aware suggestions for the things you keep meaning to do. Built for iPhone, with Apple Reminders, optional nudges, and on-device privacy.
eyebrow: Tasks, when you have time for them.
headline: Make room for the things you keep meaning to do.
intro: Whether you want to read a chapter or get something done around the house, A Good Time suggests tasks from your list that fit your available time and where you are.
hero_note: An early beta for iPhone · iOS 18 or later
now_alt: A Good Time’s Now screen suggesting Read a chapter, with its estimated time, a reason, and a Start button.
hero_caption: A suggestion with an explanation of why it fits.
principles_label: Made with your day in mind
principles: You decide when to act on a suggestion.
There are no streaks to maintain.
Your personal context stays on your device.
story_title: A task list that considers when you can use it.
story_intro: Alongside what you want to do, the app considers how long a task takes, where you can do it, and whether your calendar leaves enough time.

stories.title: Describe what you want to do.
stories.body: Write a task in your own words, or use keyboard dictation. On a supported device, the app can fill in details such as duration and place, which you can review and change before saving.
stories.aside: You can also use the form directly or bring in a task from Apple Reminders.
stories.alt: The real task editor with the sample task Read a chapter, estimated completion time, place, and effort.
stories.caption: Review the details before saving.

stories.title: Start a task and record what you get done.
stories.body: A focused session keeps the task and its completion controls together. You can mark it done, record progress on an ongoing activity, or stop and return to it later.
stories.aside: If you have a free moment, you can ask for a suggestion without waiting for an automatic nudge.
stories.alt: The practice task Stretch your shoulders is in progress, with controls to finish or stop.
stories.caption: From the notification to a finished task.

stories.title: Choose when suggestions are welcome.
stories.body: Set your welcome hours and a maximum of zero to five automatic suggestions a day. When a suggestion arrives, you can snooze it, choose something else, or leave it for another day.
stories.aside: The daily maximum is a limit, so the app may send fewer suggestions when there isn’t a suitable opportunity.
stories.alt: The suggestion preferences screen showing a daily maximum of two suggestions and weekday and weekend welcome hours.
stories.caption: Set the hours and daily maximum that suit you.

connections_title: Use the context that helps you.
connections_intro: You can connect your calendar, reminders, and other signals to make suggestions more relevant, without adding appointments to your calendar.
features: Use selected calendars to find free time around your commitments. The app retains busy and free intervals rather than event titles, descriptions, attendees, or locations.
Activate existing Apple Reminders so their titles, due dates, and completion stay in sync with the tasks you use in A Good Time.
Choose where a task can be done and, if you enable arrival suggestions, the app can check for a suitable task when you get there.
Choose apps or app categories that you associate with procrastination. When you spend time in them, A Good Time may suggest something more constructive from your task list.
The Apple Watch companion lets you request a suggestion, start a task, and record progress or completion, while your iPhone manages the task list and timing.
You can review your focused sessions and weekly progress without streaks or a score to maintain.
privacy_title: Your tasks and timing are processed on your device.
privacy_intro: A Good Time uses your task and timing context locally, without an account, analytics, or an app backend.
privacy_points: Calendar access is used for busy and free intervals, not a saved copy of your events.
Places and Screen Time are optional, so you choose which permissions to enable.
Exporting app data is an explicit choice, never an automatic upload.
privacy_note: If you connect Apple Reminders, linked reminders follow the sync settings of your chosen Apple account. This website uses no analytics or cookies; GitHub provides the hosting. Only share what is needed. Remove task names, calendar details, locations and other personal information from screenshots. Nothing is uploaded automatically. GitHub and your email provider process what you choose to send.
faqs: The TestFlight invitation isn’t available yet. This page will link directly to the beta when it opens. There’s no email signup.

You need an iPhone running iOS 18 or later; the app supports English, Italian, and Spanish. Automatic task drafting requires iOS 26 or later with Apple Intelligence available and enabled. You can use the form on other devices, and Apple Watch is optional.
Do I have to enable every permission?

No. Start by adding tasks and enable connections as they become useful. Calendar availability helps the app judge what fits; missing context can limit suggestions. Location and Screen Time remain optional.
Will it always nudge me at the right time?

It aims to find suitable moments, but suggestions depend on available context and iOS background delivery. A nudge isn’t guaranteed. You can always open the app, choose a task, or ask it to check what fits.
What should I expect from the beta?

The app is still being tested, so you may encounter bugs and changes to how suggestions work. If you’re interested in comparing timing approaches, there is also a separate, optional personal experiment in the app.
